newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS NEWS - AUGUST 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS NEWS - AUGUST 11.

DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BODY SHOP CHIEF HAS 2M OPTIONS EXTENDED

Body Shop managing director Stuart Rose has been given permission to hold on to his two million share options, which would have expired this week, for another seven years. Rose, who holds no actual shares in the company, was initially given permission by shareholders at the company's 1996 annual meeting, as it made sense to extend the options 'rather than let him exercise them and issue him with new shares'. The options have been valued at 1.4m stg.
-- SUGAR SEES BIG BARGAIN IN AMSTRAD VOUCHERS

Former Amstrad boss Alan Sugar has offered shareholders in the now- defunct computer group extra cash if they agree to relinquish to him their rights to take part in the potential legal earnings he stands to gain if successful in his legal action against two US disk-drive makers. Sugar has offered to buy the litigation vouchers at 10p each, what he claims is their current market price.
-- GEHE SELLS 55M STG MCCARTHY

Management buy-out specialist Cinven has acquired Gehe's Macarthy Group pharmaceuticals company in a 55.5m stg buy-out. Macarthy, formerly a part of the Lloyd's chemist group, was acquired by Gehe earlier in the year, and is best known for its wide range of injectable and special medicines, as well as its narcotics and opthalmics. The company employs 215 people and sells to the NHS and other leading pharmaceuticals wholesalers and retailers.
THE TIMES
-- PSION FAILS TO MEET DEMAND

Demand for Palmtop computer group Psion' Series 5 model has been so immense that the group has announced it will no longer be able to supply retailers with the 499 stg product. Psion managing director Nicholas Myers admitted the company is having 'tincy wincy production problems' due to higher than expected demand, which has led retailers to tell customers they will have to wait at least three weeks to get a Series 5 machine.
-- ANSWERING CHECHENIA'S CALL

Granger Telecom, a small Surrey telecoms firm formed in 1993, has been awarded a $300m (190m stg) contract to design and construct a new telecommunications system for the Chechen Republic. The Chechenian government believe once the radio-based system - which will offer phone access to over 95 per cent of the population - is in place, the country's potential for commercial development will have greatly improved.
-- B&Q EXPANDS ITS PRESENCE IN FAR EAST

Britain's leading do-it-yourself chain, B&Q, has made plans to further its overseas assault by opening two new branches in Taiwan. B&Q, which is owned by Kingfisher, already has one store in Taiwan and company chairman Jim Hodkinson says there could be as many as 25 branches eventually in operation. Kingfisher's current investment in the area is estimated at between 10m stg and 12m stg.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BT IS URGED TO CUT MCI MERGER BILL

British Telecom has confirmed it has received major pressure from major investors such as the Prudential, Britain's largest investment firm, and other institutions such as PFDM and Standard Life, due to concern over lack of information and rumours of 'secret' clauses in the merger agreement between it and MCI. BT denies any shareholder has outright opposed the merger and stated shareholders will be the first to learn the results of its internal review, to be completed at the end of the mo nth.
-- HEALTH TAKES A BODY BLOW FROM THE POUND

UK medical and healthcare group Smith & Nephew will announce their interim results on Tuesday, with profits expected to have dropped from 91.9m stg to between 79m stg and 89m stg. Full-year results at Smith & Nephew are expected to be 'significantly' impacted by the strength of the pound and a first half loss of 2m stg has been estimated for its Dermagraft tissue-replacement product.
-- BANK ECONOMISTS COME UP WITH A PRICE FOR INFLATION

According to a team of Bank of England economists, a two-point cut in inflation would benefit households in the country to the tune of 1.5bn stg in 1996 terms. The economists assert inflation lessens the return made on savings and investments, leading people to put less money aside for retirement and affecting the amount of money invested in housing and other areas of spending. Adjustments made to accommodate higher inflation were estimated at 0.2 per cent of GDP.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- 'DYNAMIC' DEPARTMENT STORES ROAR AHEAD

According to retail consultancy Verdict, sales at department stores grew five per cent in 1996, to 7.6bn stg, confirming the popularity of large stores is experiencing a renewed growth following a period of deep unfashionability. Sales at leading companies grew 6.6 per cent, far beyond the total retail growth of 5. 3 per cent. Over the next four years, 15 new department stores are expected to open in Britain.
-- TESCO BACK AT THE TOP TEN YEARS ON

According to the 1997 Retail Rankings report, published by Corporate Intelligence, Tesco has regained its position as the number one UK retailer, a position it last held in 1987. Corporate Intelligence figures show Tesco's retail sales were at 11.6bn stg in 1995/96, followed closely by Sainsbury at 11.2bn stg and further behind, Safeway at 6.1bn stg.
Sunglass Hut experienced the fastest sales growth in 1995/96, at 114.4 per cent, followed by Foothold and Kingway Scotland.
-- WATCHDOG INVESTIGATES TELEWEST CABLES DELAY

Telecommunications watchdog Oftel has begun an investigation into plans by cable operator Telewest to delay completion of its network for two years in an attempt to cut costs. Oftel head Don Cruickshank is worried the delays will be emulated by other cable operators such as Cable & Wireless Communications, who are also looking to save money.
